newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN SHARES SET RECORD ON LOCAL SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN SHARES SET RECORD ON LOCAL SUPPORT.

text.p: Leading Russian shares set their second consecutive record on Wednesday on local demand, traders said, adding Western interest was focused in less liquid shares.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed up 1.5 percent at a record 533.86 after Tuesday's record 526.20.
"The market is demonstrating sustained growth in the absence of practically any Western demand," said United City Bank securities chief Samit Yakovlev.

"The way Russian banks and Russian clients are going, it looks like there's no need to expect any corrections for now." Local operators have been slowly entering the equity market for months as yields on the domestic bond market have fallen.
Shares of oil company LUKoil rose to $24.90 after closing on Tuesday at $23.95 and national power company UES ticked up to $0.4400 after $0.4325.
Ordinary shares in Norilsk Nickel, one day after powerful Uneximbank won a tender for a controlling stake in the company, firmed to $15.50 after $15.15. Preferred shares rose to $13.50 from $12.60.

Rossiisky Kredit Bank head equity trader Oleg Martynenko said news that the rouble would be redenominated was still rousing demand although he said he did not expect the market to grow actively in the short term.
"This is bottom fishing for now," Martynenko said. "I think this situation will continue on the blue chip market until some event jolts it in some direction or other.
He said more active buying in stocks of St Petersburg companies which are due to be included on the RTS system.
